subject: MOVE statement
notes: kb/Work/PB425.md LANDED - GR2 is implemented as the standard writes it and the exclusion is kept beside it. THE ONE HOME is MoveClassifier.Sender(source, target): a BoundStringLiteral of length zero becomes BoundFigurative 'S' (GR2, an alphanumeric or national literal) unless the receiving operand is a dynamic-length elementary item, and the answer is computed PER RECEIVER because GR2's own exclusion is per receiver - MoveClassifier.Classify now returns a MoveStore(Sender, Kind) per target and BoundMove carries them as .Stores, so MOVE "" TO D-DYN, R-NUM empties the dynamic-length item AND space-fills the numeric one from one statement (golden conformance:cases/14.9.25-MOVE/pb425_zero_length_item_move, EXCL-LEN=00 / EXCL-NUM=[   ]). EVERY implicit MOVE inherits it by construction, because every one of them builds a BoundMove: the WRITE/REWRITE/RELEASE ... FROM and READ/RETURN ... INTO phrases through MoveBinder.BindMoveOf, and INITIALIZE's per-target implicit MOVE (14.9.20.4 GR4) through InitializeEmitter's own construction - measured: INITIALIZE g REPLACING ALPHANUMERIC DATA BY B"" now stores 000. GR1's zero-length-ITEM clause is implemented as the RUNTIME half of the same rule (MoveClassifier.ZeroLengthItemRoute): the receiver filter is a proof, not a shortcut - for every receiver category other than numeric and numeric-edited an empty sender and the substituted figurative deposit the same characters by 14.6.8.3-14.6.8.6, so a runtime test is emitted only where they differ; the sending shapes are the two runtime-length elementary ones (DYNAMIC LENGTH, ANY LENGTH) and MoveBinder freezes a reference-modified or function-identifier sender into SendingValueTemp's dynamic-length carrier first, which GR1's own 'evaluated only once' sentence requires anyway. MEASURED AFTER: MOVE "" TO PIC 9(3) stores the same three spaces MOVE SPACE TO that item stores at 85/2002/2014 (the golden asserts the EQUIVALENCE GR2 states, SAME-AS-SPACE), a DYNAMIC LENGTH item at length 0 moved to PIC 9(3) stores the same fill and at length 2 still converts (ZL-NUM=[   ] / NZ-NUM=[077]), and FUNCTION TRIM of an all-space argument does likewise (FN-ZL=[   ] / FN-NZ=[012]). THE DIAGNOSTICS STAY THE LITERAL'S, which is the half that makes the fix correct rather than merely different: 14.9.25.3 SR5/SR6/SR7 are syntax rules over a closed list of figurative constants WRITTEN in the source, so they read BoundMove.Source and never BoundMove.Stores - MOVE "" TO PIC 9(3) still COMPILES at 2023 strict where MOVE SPACE TO the same item is COBOL0902, pinned both ways by ZeroLengthLiteralMoveTests.ZeroLengthLiteral_IntoNumeric_IsNotTheSr5Removal_At2023Strict. RESIDUE, named rather than claimed: the GROUP-shaped zero-length items of 8.5.1.10 items 2, 5 and 7 (a group whose only member is a zero-length item, a zero-length variable-length record, a variable-length group of empty dynamic tables) do not take GR1's route - they send through 14.9.25.4 GR4's group move, whose kind GR1 would itself change, and SendingValueTemp's recorded non-materialization of a variable-length group (row GR-14.9.25.4-1) is the same boundary. FINISHER (kb/Work PB425, wave 39): GR1's antecedent is CONDITIONAL - 'If identifier-1 IS a zero-length item' - and 8.5.4's enumeration makes the two sending shapes whose length is not a stable field read conditional in turn, so MoveClassifier.CanBeZeroLengthItem now gates the freeze. 8.5.4 item 9 is a reference-modified data item 'when that has been permitted by use of the compiler directive REF-MOD-ZERO-LENGTH' (outside such a region 7.3.23.3 GR1 raises EC-BOUND-REF-MOD, so GR1's antecedent can never hold), and 8.5.4 item 6 is 'an intrinsic function that returns a zero-length value' - never a NUMERIC one, whose returned value 15.4 puts in a temporary elementary data item with at least one digit position. Freezing on the SHAPE alone was a wrong answer, not a wasted temp: a numeric function sender was hoisted into SendingValueTemp.FunctionValuePic (21 integer + 9 fraction digits), narrower than a STANDARD-DECIMAL or float result, so MOVE FUNCTION E TO a 31-digit item stored 2718281828000000000000000000000 for 2718281828459045235360287471352 - eight corpus cases measured RED before and GREEN after (pb65_dec_move_channel, pb60_numvalf_native_channels, pb60_numval_standard_decimal, pb251_numval_native_value_fixed, pb253_prose_float_standard_container x3 editions, l1_numval_family_cap_discriminators). The inherited 8.5.1.10 citations for the zero-length-item ENUMERATION were re-derived and repaired to 8.5.4 in the same change set (8.5.1.10 is Dynamic-length elementary items and does not contain the words 'zero-length item'). retired-witness: conformance:2002/pb425_zero_length_literal_move (the golden moved to the 2014 corpus: it writes a zero-length literal, a COBOL-2014 introduction gated by kb/Work PB895 (same program, same expected output)) retired-witness: conformance-test:ZeroLengthLiteralMoveTests.ZeroLengthLiteral_IntoNumeric_IsNotTheSr5Removal_At2023Strict (kb/Work PB3605: renamed ZeroLengthLiteral_IntoNumeric_IsNotRefusedBySr5 and run at 85 and 2023, since the written SPACE it contrasts with is refused at every edition, not only at 2023)
